title: The ARKAY label and leaving the record business
summary: Rose explains he sold the Burley masters to Exclusive because distribution and disc jockey promotion were too cumbersome; ARKAY had a nominal partner named Kessler.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well, back to, uh, the actual recording session itself. Uh, how did that go with Burley? Well, very well.

It was, uh, it was a very successful session and, uh, sold well. And because of the fact that I really couldn't be... I found that being involved in the record business was, uh, more demanding than I expected. I, uh, sold the masters to Exclusive, who then reissued them on their label.
Well, but what label were they on originally?

That was called R-K, A-R-K-A-Y. Mm-hmm. And, uh, the, uh, it was just too cumbersome. We made four sides and that was about all. I mean, I really couldn't handle the distribution factors. And I found that I really didn't want to be bothered with it, is what it is.
Were you, uh, did, were you owner of R-K?

Yeah, well, I was, I was actually the owner. But we set up a corporate structure with my then business partner, uh, whose name was Kessler, and we just used the initials of R-K. And, uh, but he was not really involved in it at all. I just, uh, had him on as a member of a corporation, because I needed to incorporate.
Well, was there, did you have to call on disc jockeys, or? Yeah.
Yeah. I did all that. Paying all that? Yes, and I found that I didn't care very much for it. So, uh, I discovered how Simi, that side of the record business was, and I just got out of it.
